extracted.intended_audience: educated reading public; patrons and practitioners of monuments, sign-makers, and composers
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive aesthetic guidance for public monuments, epitaphs, shop signs, and musical recitative (from The Spectator essays). Covers what inscriptions, iconography, and musical settings should do to suit character, trade, language, and public taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extravagant epitaphic praise
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of them were covered with such extravagant Epitaphs, that, if it were possible for the dead Person to be acquainted with them, he would blush at the Praises which his Friends have bestowed upon him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: excessively inflated compliments that do not match the deceased's life. Example given: monuments that praise beyond merit. Scoring note: prefer modest, truthful eulogy over hyperbole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit public monuments and inscriptions to learned review
rubrics_metrics.description: they should be submitted to the Perusal of Men of Learning and Genius before they are put in Execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Have scholars or men of taste vet phrasing and symbolism prior to erection. Prevents vulgar mistakes in language, style, or symbolism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monument should represent the subject's true character and deeds
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of the brave rough English Admiral, which was the distinguishing Character of that plain gallant Man, he is represented on his Tomb by the Figure of a Beau ... The Inscription ... acquaints us only with the Manner of his Death, in which it was impossible for him to reap any Honour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: imagery and inscription must match the individual's distinguishing qualities and celebrate meaningful actions (not irrelevant details like manner of death). Anti-pattern: elegant but misleading portraiture that contradicts the person's life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use profession-appropriate iconography on monuments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Monuments of their Admirals ... represent them like themselves; and are adorned with rostral Crowns and naval Ornaments, with beautiful Festoons of [Seaweed], Shells, and Coral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: choose symbols that have a clear relation to the subject's life or profession (naval motifs for admirals). This increases antiquity/taste and public intelligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epitaphs should be elegant and just in thought
rubrics_metrics.description: I could not but be very much delighted with several modern Epitaphs, which are written with great Elegance of Expression and Justness of Thought, and therefore do Honour to the Living as well as to the Dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring: value inscriptions for clarity, felicitous expression, and fair-minded judgement. Good epitaphs honor both memory and the living community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inscriptions in obscure languages that render them inaccessible
rubrics_metrics.description: There are others so excessively modest, that they deliver the Character of the Person departed in Greek or Hebrew, and by that Means are not understood once in a Twelve-month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: inscriptions should be accessible to the intended public; overly learned or obscure language defeats the communicative purpose of a monument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fantastical or monstrous sign imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: My first Task, therefore, should be, like that of Hercules, to clear the City from Monsters. ... Our streets are filled with blue Boars, black Swans, and red Lions; not to mention flying Pigs, and Hogs in Armour, with many other Creatures more extraordinary than any in the desarts of Africk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: invention of bizarre, meaningless creatures on signs. Preference for recognisable, sober devices that do not confuse or scandalize viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit jarring or incongruous combinations on a single sign
rubrics_metrics.description: I would forbid, that Creatures of jarring and incongruous Natures should be joined together in the same Sign; such as the Bell and the Neats-tongue, the Dog and Gridiron.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: ensure internal coherence of composite sign motifs; avoid arbitrary quarterings that mix unrelated objects or ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shop sign should bear affinity to the wares sold
rubrics_metrics.description: I would enjoin every Shop to make use of a Sign which bears some Affinity to the Wares in which it deals. What can be more inconsistent, than to see a Bawd at the Sign of the Angel, or a Taylor at the Lion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: semantic match between sign and trade (e.g., fish for a fishmonger). Anti-patterns highlighted (misleading or ironic pairings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow name-derived or ingenious devices where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Name gives an Occasion for an ingenious Sign-post, I would likewise advise the Owner to take that Opportunity of letting the World know who he is. ... Mrs. Salmon ... has erected before her House the Figure of the Fish that is her Namesake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: puns or name-devices (rebus) are encouraged when they meaningfully identify the proprietor and lend wit, provided they do not misrepresent the trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish sensible rules for quartering or adopting another's sign
rubrics_metrics.description: It is usual for a young Tradesman, at his first setting up, to add to his own Sign that of the Master whom he serv'd; ... This I take to have given Rise to many of those Absurdities ... I would, therefore, establish certain Rules, for the determining how far one Tradesman may 'give' the Sign of another, and in what Cases he may be allowed to quarter it with his own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: limit and regulate the practice of combining or appropriating others' devices to prevent incoherent, crowded, or misleading signage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signage communicates the occupant's humour or character
rubrics_metrics.description: I can give a shrewd Guess at the Humour of the Inhabitant by the Sign that hangs before his Door. A surly cholerick Fellow generally makes Choice of a Bear, as Men of milder Dispositions, frequently live at the Lamb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation as evaluative principle: designers should be aware signs are read as personality cues; select imagery that conveys the intended disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recitative and musical setting must suit the accent/tone of the language
rubrics_metrics.description: For this Reason, the Recitative Musick in every Language, should be as different as the Tone or Accent of each Language; ... The only Fault I find in our present Practice, is the making use of Italian Recitative with English Words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule for composers/productions: do not graft a foreign recitative style onto a different language without adaptation; the musical cadences should reflect native speech patterns to avoid misinterpreted dramatic action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt foreign musical forms with gentle deviations for national genius
rubrics_metrics.description: an English Composer should not follow the Italian Recitative too servilely, but make use of many gentle Deviations from it, in Compliance with his own Native Language. ... allow the Italian Opera to lend our English Musick as much as may grace and soften it, but never entirely to annihilate and destroy it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: borrow graces and modulations from foreign schools to improve native music, but preserve elements that suit national taste and speech. Scoring: value adaptations that harmonize foreign technique with local sensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art's rules should be deduced from public taste, not only from art's internal principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Musick, Architecture, and Painting, as well as Poetry, and Oratory, are to deduce their Laws and Rules from the general Sense and Taste of Mankind, and not from the Principles of those Arts themselves; or, in other Words, the Taste is not to conform to the Art, but the Art to the Taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level evaluative principle: prioritize audience reception and national habits when formulating artistic rules. 'Harmony' is relative — what pleases one culture may offend another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the same language-attunement rule to songs and airs
rubrics_metrics.description: The same Observations which I have made upon the Recitative part of Musick may be applied to all our Songs and Airs in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: composers of songs and airs should fit melodic contours and cadences to the prosody and accentuation of the language in which lyrics are sung.
